title: ‘We’re definitely in the fight’ says Dunne after race-winning Baku weekend
excerpt:
Alexander Dunne was admittedly slightly disappointed with how his weekend in Baku ended but acknowledged what a positive few days he and Rodin Motorsport had in Azerbaijan.

The Irish driver impressively took pole position in Qualifying 1 and achieved podiums in all three races – including a victory in Feature Race 1.

Dunne also took the chequered flag first in the second Feature Race but a five-second time penalty for crossing the while line ahead of pit lane entry dropped him to third in the classification.

Reflecting on it all, Dunne admitted being a bit downbeat about Saturday’s result, but took plenty of positives from a strong three days of running.

“When you look at it as a whole, it was a pretty spectacular weekend,” said Dunne. “But after the penalty in the Feature Race, I left the weekend a bit upset and a bit disappointed.

“That is not something I ever thought I would say considering I had a pole, a front row for the second Feature Race, and three out of three podiums.

Dunne was downbeat at the end of the weekend after missing out on victory in Feature Race 2

“If you offered me that as a whole before the weekend had started, I would have absolutely taken it. Still, naturally, it's a standard racing driver thing that there was an opportunity for a little bit more, so I was a bit disappointed.

“But if you look back on it as a whole, the weekend was super strong. The team did a great job. The car was really, really strong in all conditions. In FP, we were really quick, in quali, we were quick, and all three races, we were fast as well.

READ MORE

‘It was much more than a win’ says Tsolov after comeback to second in Baku Feature Race 2

Title fight ‘far from over’ says Câmara after taking the lead in Baku

“In terms of feeling and car performance, you can't really ask for a whole lot more. Apart from the penalty, in terms of pace and driving-wise on track, I was able to maximise what they gave me as well, which of course is always the goal when the car is good.”

Looking back at Feature Race 1, Dunne achieved his first victory of the season with a dominant performance, winning by 4.3s to teammate Martinius Stenshorne.

Starting from pole is not always a guaranteed place for success around Baku with the long DRS straights, but Dunne felt he and the team handled things well.

Dunne was impressed with the performance of the car all weekend

“The Supersoft stint was particularly strong,” he explained. "In general, the Supersoft, the softer compound of tyre stints normally is something that I'm quite good at, and I was able to capitalise on that quite a lot in the first Feature Race.

“I probably expected it to be a little bit harder and to have a bit more of a fight with Martinius. I expected there to be a little bit more of a battle and for it to be more difficult to get out of DRS, but I had a good start.

“Martinius and Noel were fighting with each other, which gave me a little bit of a gap, and then once I realised there was a chance to break DRS, I pushed quite hard in the first couple of laps. Once I had broken DRS, I tried to settle into the rhythm and the pace seemed to be really strong.”

Strategy in Feature Race 2 was slightly more complicated for the drivers, especially Dunne, who chose to pit early anticipating a Virtual Safety Car.

But the Irishman felt his place out on track, having been P2 behind Stenshorne, made things more complicated for him and the team, as it was an earlier stop than he had wanted.

“In terms of tyre feeling and raw pace in the second Feature Race, I would have liked to have stayed out,” he revealed. “But the fact that Martinius and I were P1 and P2, it makes the strategy a bit more difficult for both of us, because we can't pit at the same time.

Dunne talked through the strategy call in Feature Race 2 and having to pit early

“So when I saw that Martinius wasn't pitting on that lap, to me it seemed like a good opportunity to try and capitalise and come to the pits and save myself a bit of time.

“If I was in his position in the lead, then I probably would have stayed out for a little bit longer.”

READ MORE

Tuukka Taponen steps up with ART Grand Prix for the 2027 season

FEATURE RACE 2: Câmara inherits victory and leads championship after Baku

Dunne leaves Baku in a much stronger position in the title fight than when he came to the weekend. He was 38 points adrift of the leader but is now just 18 behind heading into the final two rounds.

“We're definitely in the fight,” he added. “But I'm not necessarily going to shift my focus onto the championship. I think three or four rounds ago, I completely switched off from the idea of winning the championship.

“I just focused round by round to try and pick up a good result, and on trying to get the first win of the year, which I'm very happy we managed to get it in Baku.

Dunne believes he is firmly in the title fight heading into the final two rounds

“After the first Feature Race, when I was talking with my dad, I couldn't believe that I was within eight points of the lead. I couldn't believe that we had brought the gap down from 60 points in the space of two weekends.

“So for me, I still want to keep the focus on having as many strong weekends as possible. I'd also really like to try and keep up the qualifying form. That’s something that for myself and the team has been really impressive all year.

“If we can try and keep up that, I'd be really happy, and then we will see where we end up.”

title: ‘It was much more than a win’ says Tsolov after comeback to second in Baku Feature Race 2
excerpt:
Nikola Tsolov went from P11 to second in Baku Feature Race 2 and was extremely proud of his and Campos Racing's efforts

Nikola Tsolov says his and Campos Racing’s fightback over the course of the Baku weekend is something he will carry for the rest of his life.

The Bulgarian driver and his team struggled for much of Round 12, finishing fifth in the Sprint Race, before losing the lead of the championship for the first time in Feature Race 1.

But Tsolov and Campos recovered on Saturday, going from 11th to second in Feature Race 2, and speaking at the end of the weekend, he admitted that it’s a result that will live long in his memory.

“It's a really positive day,” he said. “I think more so than just the good result, I think the way we managed to bounce back.

“From being almost the slowest in the Sprint Race to being the quickest today just shows our spirit and how we worked within the team to turn around things.

“For me it's important that we never gave up and this is just a test of life that we managed to pass, and this is only going to make us a lot stronger.

Tsolov drove an impressive race from P11 to second to keep his title hopes alive

“I think having managed to overcome this and still work in the right direction with the team is something that we can take on to the rest of the year and really come back much stronger.”

Feature Race 2 did not get off to the best of starts for Tsolov, as he was stuck in the midfield for much of the first stint in P10.

READ MORE

Title fight ‘far from over’ says Câmara after taking the lead in Baku

Tuukka Taponen steps up with ART Grand Prix for the 2027 season

But an inspired strategy call from the Bulgarian and his team to stay out longer in the first stint despite two Virtual Safety Cars saw him come back out in P5.

“The tyres felt good all the way through,” he said. “Then with the VSCs I managed to cool them down a little bit and that really helped the Supersoft to stay in the good window.

“The pace was just strong, so we managed to pull the gap that we lost out to people who pitted before the VSC. I was to be quite surprised when we went out pretty far ahead and I got told that we were virtually P5 when I came out of the pit.

Tsolov praised the fighting spirit of his Campos Racing team

“I was surprised and really happy to hear. From then on, we were just taking it step-by-step, lap-by-lap and I was really in my own race, in my own tunnel let's say.”

Tsolov overtook Laurens van Hoepen and Martinius Stenshorne to get up to third and chased down Câmara and Alexander Dunne in the closing stages – getting to within DRS range of the former.

Talking about his mindset in the final few laps, the Campos driver says there was not a lot on his mind at the time.

“There was no thought process of what was going on ahead,” he said. “It was more about what I could do in driving to make the best out of the situation.

“So I was just thinking how to manage the tyres by going as quick as I can, really focusing on what I was doing. I actually don't remember most of the race because I was really in the tunnel, really focused, and you don't think about anything.”

The Bulgarian says his P2 result feels like a victory

Despite losing the championship lead for the first time since Silverstone, Tsolov views his Baku weekend as a positive, given the fighting spirit shown by him and Campos.

FEATURE RACE 2: Câmara inherits victory and leads championship after Baku

“It was much more than a win,” he added. “I think this is something that I can take on for the rest of my life and I think everyone in the team can as well.

“It’s really inspiring to see what we were able to do and how quick we turned things around and the fact that we never gave up, so this is more than a win for sure.”

title: Title fight ‘far from over’ says Câmara after taking the lead in Baku
excerpt:
Rafael Câmara gave his view on his victory in Baku Feature Race, taking the title lead and the battle against Nikola Tsolov and Alexander Dunne

Rafael Câmara took victory of the Baku Feature Race 2 and with it, left a race weekend with the championship lead for the first time season.

The Invicta Racing driver had a strong few days in Azerbaijan, qualifying in the top five for both races, before finishing fourth in Feature Race 1 after a drag race to the line with Noel León.

That result on Friday afternoon earned Câmara lead of the championship over Nikola Tsolov by one point, and he extended it to seven on Saturday morning.

The Brazilian driver took the chequered flag in second but gained a place at the line once Alexander Dunne’s five-second time penalty took effect.

This means Câmara leaves a race weekend at the top of the Standings going to Lusail, but he is not taking anything for granted.

“It feels good,” he said on leading the championship. “It’s my first time leading this championship this whole season, and it was good to get the win to extend the gap.

The Invicta driver was forced to chase down Dunne for much of the Feature Race 2

“We know that it's still far from over, but we will still keep working hard to make sure that we are ready for every scenario moving forward.”

Câmara finished ahead of title rival Nikola Tsolov, after the two used the same strategy. With Ritomo Miyata having stopped on track, many drivers, including Dunne who was leading, opted to make their mandatory stop anticipating a Virtual Safety Car.

READ MORE

Tuukka Taponen steps up with ART Grand Prix for the 2027 season

FEATURE RACE 2: Câmara inherits victory and leads championship after Baku

Câmara chose to stay out, as he did when the second VSC was signalled with Tasanapol Inthraphuvasak having pulled over to the side of the road.

The Invicta driver came in once racing conditions returned and both title hopefuls made gains on their rivals, although Câmara admitted he was not convinced it was the right call at the time.

“On that side I thought that we actually made a mistake, but the pace was looking very strong after the VSC,” he said.

This was Câmara's third Feature Race victory of the season

“I think because of that we were able to come back ahead. I think that was very important for the whole race. I think overall everything went well today but we were just missing a bit of pace to try something and get the win on track.”

While trying to make a move on Dunne ahead, Câmara was also forced to defend from the charging Tsolov in the final stages.

The Ferrari Driver Academy member revealed what he was thinking as his Campos Racing rival closed in.

“I saw Nikola coming and he was quick,” he continued. “Luckily, it was just not enough to get us. He was looking very strong. Also Alex was doing a good job.

“In the beginning we were just trying to be there to try something in the end. I knew he had the five second penalty, so I knew that I could actually wait a bit and see how things were and try again. I really tried in the end, but it was just not enough to stay.

The Brazilian does not believe the title fight with Tsolov and Dunne is over despite him taking the lead in the Standings

“But even with that I've been a bit lucky, he finished second and we got the win. So for the championship it was very good.”

On the title fight, the top three are covered by 18 points going into Lusail, and Câmara sees some similarities with his 2025 Formula 3 title-winning campaign.

Round 12 Post-Feature Race 2 Press Conference

Dino Beganovic: 'A great result and deserved reward' following another Baku podium

“I mean, it's very close,” he said on the fight. “It’s probably now quite a bit similar to last year, being the one that is being chased.

“But anyway, I think whatever the situation, we just really focus on what we can do in the best way. This will be the target for the last two rounds, to really try to maximise what we can.

“I think they are two tracks that are very strong for the team. So we will try to keep it up and finish in a good way.”

title: Tuukka Taponen steps up with ART Grand Prix for the 2027 season
excerpt:
ART Grand Prix have announced the signing of Tuukka Taponen for the 2027 FIA Formula 2 season.

Taponen graduates to F2 after a stellar 2026 campaign in Formula 3 where he scored three podiums, including one victory, two Pole Positions and finished third in the Drivers' Championship.

Prior to that, the 19-year-old raced with ART in his rookie year in F3, and they achieved three podiums in the 2025 campaign.

Before racing in Formula 3, Taponen won the 2024 Formula Regional Middle East Championship title and wound up third in the European leg of the competition.

For 2027, Taponen will step up to Formula 2, and he is excited to be doing so in a team he knows well.

“I believe we have a good chance of fighting for the front positions right away," said Taponen. "ART is a team I know well, and I know how they work. F2 will introduce a new car version next season, along with regulation changes, which will level the playing field for all teams.

"It's also great to return to a team that already knows me and wanted me back. I'm confident I'll get the support I need from the team to take this next step and pursue my goal of reaching Formula 1.”

ART Grand Prix Team Principal Sébastien Philippe added: "I’m very happy to have Tuukka back in the team! We are already a step ahead, having built a solid foundation and a strong relationship together in the past. This allows us to focus fully, from the outset, on his performance and the development of the car”.

title: Round 12 Post-Feature Race 2 Press Conference
excerpt:
FIA Formula 2: Hello and welcome to today's FIA Formula 2 Press Conference following the Feature Race here at the Baku City Circuit. Joining us this morning: in third place, Alexander Dunne for Rodin Motorsport; in second place, Nikola Tsolov for Campos Racing; and the winner of today's race, Rafael Câmara for Invicta Racing. Starting with you, Rafa, congratulations. This is your third win this season. It was a race that took a lot of twists and turns. Can you tell us about it?

Rafael Câmara: Yeah, I mean, it was a long race for me, all the way behind Alex. I think on the Supersoft, in the first stint, we were quite good, but after that, every time I was getting close to Alex, it was tricky to follow behind. Then it was difficult to get a chance into Turn 1. Overall, it was very good because he had a penalty, but it felt like we won a bit more, and it was a bit tricky today.

FIA Formula 2: You mentioned that you were informed there was a five-second time penalty for Alex. How much did that affect your ability to try to pass him, or did it mean playing it safer?

Câmara: Probably at the beginning of the stint I could try a bit as well with the good tyres, but after that, even if I tried, I couldn't overtake him. I think he was just better overall. It was tricky to follow and get close enough to try something, but in the end it was a very good weekend for us in terms of the championship. Yesterday we also scored what we could, and I think it was a positive weekend overall.

FIA Formula 2: You have extended your championship lead heading into the next round. That was the objective coming into the round, but at any point during this weekend did you think it might be difficult, or was it a given?

Câmara Not really. I knew it was a new track, a street circuit, but looking at the past years, the team has always been good here. I knew that by doing the work beforehand and preparing well, we could be there fighting for both positions in the races. In the end, we were quite strong from FP. In qualifying, I think we were always there. Overall, throughout the weekend, we always had a chance to be fighting, so I think it was a very positive weekend, even though it was a new track. Now we just keep working and see what happens in the final two rounds.

FIA Formula 2: Congratulations for today. Moving on to you, Nikola. It is P2 after starting from 11th. You must be quite pleased with that comeback today?

Nikola Tsolov: Yeah, overall I am pleased with the result, but I am more pleased with what we did, to be honest. It has been a tough couple of rounds, and especially this weekend we did not have the pace at all. Starting the Sprint from pole, usually whenever we are in the top three or top five, we are fighting for the win, and it has been really hard on me and hard on the team. But we never gave up, and that is what I am really proud of. All the hard work we have put in to improve the car every round, and especially this weekend, and the step we have made, for me this is more than a win. Personally, this is a fight with ourselves that we have been having, and we have overcome it. We have overcome a lot of tough moments this year, so I am really proud of what we have done as a team, and I am happy to be here.

FIA Formula 2: The decision to stay out during the VSC proved crucial. What were you discussing with the team during those moments? It worked perfectly for you.

Tsolov: We were prepared to pit every time there was a VSC, but I ended up passing the pit entry line each time before it was deployed. It was just the situation. To be honest, I thought we would lose time, but in the end we were really fast on the Supersoft in the first stint. Staying out gave us the advantage of extending while cooling down the tyres and having better grip. Then I was really surprised when they told me, 'It is looking good. You are coming out virtually P5.' I was like, 'Oh, we are actually in the fight.' At that point I was pretty happy to hear that. From there, I just built on it. I had a lot of pace, and trying to catch these two guys was difficult, but I managed to arrive in the end.

FIA Formula 2: You mentioned it was difficult to catch them, but you looked very quick towards the end of the race. Did you think at any moment that you could fight these two for the win?

Tsolov: Maybe with five laps to go, but I thought they were a bit too far away to catch. Then, when Alex started to struggle a little more, Rafa got the DRS, so at that point I thought it was going to be harder. Even if I caught them, I thought it would be hard to pass Rafa because passing Martinius, who was much slower and without DRS, was very difficult. I knew it was going to be really tough, and I accepted both situations at that point. I was prepared for everything, but deep inside I always pushed to get that last bit. Obviously, with Rafa, I was going to risk a little more to overtake if it came to that point.

FIA Formula 2: Thank you very much. Good job today. Alex, moving on to you. It is P3, but you led across the line at the chequered flag. It is probably a bittersweet podium, but you were impressive all weekend. How do you reflect on that race and the weekend overall?

Alexander Dunne: I do not know. I just want to go home, to be honest. No, it has been a really good weekend. We were on the front row for both races, took pole, and I won both races on track. Apart from one silly little mistake, in terms of driving and on my side, I do not think I left much out there, which is what I said I would do at the beginning of the weekend. The car was really good all weekend, and the team really turned it around. Today we probably struggled a little more, but it is not going to be perfect every time. I think I still managed to hang on pretty well, and the car was good enough to hang on, even though we were struggling in front of Rafa and Nikola towards the end. Ultimately, as far as weekends go, I think it was pretty good.

FIA Formula 2: Were you surprised when you came out of the pit lane behind Martinius and Rafael after the pit stop? You looked to have gained some time during the VSC.

Dunne: Yeah, I was a little bit confused because I was in the pit lane when the VSC came out, and from what I was told, I had gained quite a bit, but it did not really seem to look that way. Maybe my out-lap was a bit slower, or maybe they had really strong pace for the next couple of laps on the supersoft. I am not sure what was happening, but in the end it worked out okay. I managed to get Martinius straight away, and I got past Rafa with the DRS because he was on cold tyres. It was definitely more difficult than what had been explained at the time, but it was not too bad.

FIA Formula 2: You finished the weekend strongly and are third in the standings, with the gap not being that large. You must believe you can get closer to these two drivers next to you in the points.

Dunne: That is the plan. I am going to give it everything and try my best to close the gap. It is obviously going to be difficult. Today I saw it as a good opportunity to score points, and when I looked in my mirrors, I definitely did not expect to see Nikola in P3. I think it is pretty cool in the sense that, coming into this race, we were all pretty close on points, and even though we all started in completely different places, we are all here in the top three. It shows how high the level is and how close the championship is. Wherever we end up finishing, I am sure it will be an interesting one.

FIA Formula 2: Thank you very much. Great job this weekend.

title: Dino Beganovic: 'A great result and deserved reward' following another Baku podium
excerpt:
It was two podiums from two on Friday in Baku for Dino Beganovic. After claiming victory in the Sprint Race, he returned to the podium in Feature Race 1, finishing third behind the two Rodin Motorsport teammates.

Reflecting on his day in the paddock, the DAMS Lucas Oil driver was very enthusiastic about his and the team's performance levels on Friday in Azerbaijan.

"Very satisfied, it was a great day. Super happy with it. It was a tough day as well. Starting from this morning I was not feeling well. A lot of visits to the bathroom, but it all paid off. A very good day. Super happy for myself, for my team and a very good haul of points."

Beganovic started Feature Race 1 from eighth on the grid but made quick progress through the pack in the early stages.

The Safety Car timing was fortuitous as he admits, but a strong result was on the cards regardless as he and the team continued to show impressive speed in Baku.

He highlighted the race restarts as a particular strength and an element that made a big difference in the end result.

"Racing here - it's not over if you qualify outside the top places. You can still do a good job. There's always going to be a little bit of carnage. You've just got to be clever making the moves and taking it step by step.

Beganovic is hopeful of another charge through the pack on Saturday in the second Feature Race

"The Safety Car was great timing for us. I've been lucky on that and it definitely made our race a lot easier. After that, I think we made some good moves on the restarts. Every time into Turn 1 we were ready to gain a place.

"I think we were really strong in all the restarts. Then the Rodin boys were very quick today. It was hard to follow Martinus when he got past. I'm happy to have kept León behind after our contact. I also got some damage on my rear. Overall, I'm very satisfied."

Beganovic had a slightly tougher task on his hands tomorrow, with his Qualifying 2 result leaving him outside the top 10 for Saturday's Feature.

Still, the Ferrari Driver Academy talent is hopeful of another charge through the order, but underlines the need to stay out of trouble and make the most of opportunities as they arrive, rather than force the issue.

"Obviously, it's not going to be as easy tomorrow. It's going to be quite tough starting from 12th place.

"We've just got to do what we can do, Not invent anything and just do our race. I think we have the pace to move forward. But starting from 12th, everything becomes a lot more difficult."

title: Round 12 Post Feature Race 1 Press Conference
excerpt:
__FIA Formula 2: Welcome to the Press Conference following today's first Feature Race at the Baku City Circuit. Joining us for this press conference, in third place, Dino Beganovic for DAMS Lucas Oil, in second place, Martinius Stenshorne for Rodin Motorsport, and also from Rodin Motorsport, first time Feature Race winner Alexander Dunne. Alex, starting with you, well done. Your first victory of the year. It must feel like a long time coming, but just how pleased are you with the win and your performance overall today? __

Alexander Dunne: Yeah, it's safe to say I'm pretty happy. I mean, it's nice. To be honest, there were times in the year when I questioned whether or not it was even going to happen. So, I think for the pace to have been so strong so far this weekend, not only to have won but to have finished on the podium in the Sprint Race as well, I think so far we couldn't have really asked for much more. The team have done a really good job in turning it around. The pace last weekend and the pace so far this weekend has been phenomenal. So, I think as nice as it is for myself, just as much credit should go to them as it should to me.

FIA Formula 2: The Safety Car worked out in your favour, but how do you handle the red flags when you've been in the zone and have to step out of the car, reset and then get back in it again?

Dunne: I was quite happy there were Red Flags, to be honest, because I really needed to go to the toilet before I started the race. So, I did the same thing in Qualifying, so maybe a toilet break during or just before each session seems to work pretty well. So, no, for me it didn't change a whole lot. I think you kind of just reset and go again. So, it didn't change the world for me, to be honest.

FIA Formula 2: You're well and truly back in the frame for the lead in the Championship leaving Baku. Starting from the front row tomorrow, you must be feeling pretty good about your chances.

Dunne: Yeah, we're solidly back in the fight, which is really nice. To be honest, three or four rounds ago, I completely switched off from the Championship and, as far as I was concerned, there was no way of even getting close. But now we're more than close. So, I think game on, and I'll try and get the most out of it tomorrow.

FIA Formula 2: Thank you very much. Congratulations on a great day today. Martinius, moving on to you, it's P2 and a one-two for your team. You had to fight your way back to the second step on the podium. Talk us through your race, because you made some big overtakes throughout.

Martinius Stenshorne: Yeah, I think our race was really good. The pace was good. We had some good overtakes and some good restarts. It was a bit unfortunate that the Safety Car came out right after the box, so I lost some positions there and gained them back, and then the red flag put me back again. So, I had to do some overtaking this race, but luckily we got it done.

FIA Formula 2: It's been a very strong weekend for Rodin so far: one-two in the Feature Race and one-two in both Qualifying sessions. You and Alex have looked so quick all weekend. Is there anything specific that has worked for you at Baku?

Stenshorne: Well, I think the team has done a great job giving both me and Alex a good car. It's not always that you can have a car that can put it on pole position and win races. So, a big thank you to them. I think me and Alex are doing a good job as well to deliver these results, but a big thank you to the team for giving us a really good car.

FIA Formula 2: With what you've learned since Qualifying and how things worked out in the first Feature Race, it will be your turn to start from pole position tomorrow. You must be feeling good about your chances to win it tomorrow, correct?

Stenshorne: Yeah, I feel good. I think we had a good Sprint Race this morning as well, gaining some positions and showing good pace. We have to see how the race plays out. A lot of stuff can happen. We just have to see how it goes, but I'm confident for tomorrow that we can bring home another good result for the team.

FIA Formula 2: Thank you. Good job today. Dino, thank you for waiting. It's P3 for you. After winning the Sprint Race earlier today, you were able to use the Safety Car to your advantage. Tell us about your race this afternoon and how it was from the car.

Dino Beganovic: Yeah, first of all, it was a great day. I think, in general, from this morning to the afternoon, we knew we were strong, but it wasn't on my bingo card to have another podium today. I think it was a good race. Obviously, we made some moves at the beginning, at the race start and on all the restarts, and then we got that Safety Car at the perfect time when we wanted to box, so we got a bit lucky there. Then, after that, we were able to execute it well. Both Alex and Martinius were very strong, so I couldn't keep up with them, but in general I'm very happy with today.

FIA Formula 2: It was pole position for you in Madrid and back-to-back wins from Madrid to this morning, and another podium this afternoon. You've been very competitive over the past few rounds. It's been tough to get to that point. What changed? What has put you at this level of competitiveness right now?

Beganovic: I'm not sure. Obviously, Madrid was new for everybody, and it was a street track that I normally feel comfortable with. But other than that, I had a good summer break. After that, we have just worked well with the team. We also had some solid rounds before the summer break as well, so it's very nice to have that result in the bag now and carry on that streak. Hopefully, we can finish this weekend off well tomorrow as well.

FIA Formula 2: We see Alex closing the gap to the people in front of him in the standings. You're currently fifth and also closing in. Is a top-three finish on the cards for you?

Beganovic: Mathematically, yes, but I will be realistic and say it will be tough to get there. We need to be at our best, and a little bit more, for every weekend and every session. I'm not going to exclude it. We will do our best, and then we will see where we arrive and just try to get all the points that we have on the table.

FIA Formula 2: Thank you very much, Dino.

title: Nikola Tsolov handed grid penalty for Baku Feature Race 2
excerpt:
Following the conclusion of the FIA Formula 2 Feature Race in Baku, Nikola Tsolov has been handed a grid penalty.

During the race, Tsolov was adjujed to have crossed over the white line separating the pitlane from the trck in violation of ISC Apex L Ch IV 4(d).

The Stewards examined video evidence and found that Tsolov crossed the pit entry line with his right wheels by about one meter, and as such chose the lesser of the penalties in the guidelines, which is five seconds.

But with the driver of Car 6 having retired from the race, his penalty went unserved, and it has therefore been converted into a grid drop of three places for Feature Race 2.

Tsolov is now set to start Saturday’s race from P11.

title: Villagómez aiming for more on Saturday after drive to P8 in ‘crazy’ Baku Feature Race 1
excerpt:
Rafael Villagómez was pleased to finish P8 in the Baku Feature Race 1 and is aiming for more on Sunday

Rafael Villagómez survived a potential race exit to come through the field and finish eighth in the Baku Feature Race 1.

The Van Amersfoort Racing driver started the race from 16th and maintained that position for the early part of the race, before being involved in a multi-car collision.

At the Safety Car restart, Villagómez was part of a group of drivers that collided at Turn 3, but while the rest had to retire, the Mexican was able to bring his car back into the pitlane.

The VAR driver started from the back of the field in P14 but immediately overtook Emerson Fittipaldi.

Villagómez then picked his way through the rest of the pack to get into the points, taking the chequered flag in P9 before gaining a place once Kush Maini’s five-second penalty took effect.

Speaking in the paddock afterwards, Villagómez said: "It was crazy. At one point I was out of the race. But the team did great. I just stayed in the car and that's allowed.

“I knew I had some front wing damage, but not enough to stop, and we just went back. We knew since this morning the pace was strong, but at the back we were just so messy, anything can happen.

“We were involved in unlucky situations in both of the races today. But at the end of the day, today where the points matter, we managed to get some.”

READ MORE

FEATURE RACE 1: Dunne back in title hunt with assured Baku victory

Roman Bilinski on attacking Baku comeback: 'Sometimes you have to send it'

Villagómez was 17th in Qualifying 1 and 13th in Qualifying 2, but in both races has managed to make his way forward.

The VAR driver feels he and the team were unlucky on Thursday but knew they had the potential to do well in the races.

“In Qualifying we were really unlucky because we were one of the last ones in the pit lane,” said Villagómez. “So we always got a yellow flag in the T1 or some traffic.

The Mexican driver is aiming to score more points on Saturday

“Actually I didn't do any laps in Quali 1. Then Quali 2, basically we got lucky one lap and that was what I got for qualifying. So it was a shame because we knew the pace was much better.

“The racing is what matters and we had the pace in the race, so that's good. I don't really know what happened in the incident. If you ask me, all I know is I had a front wing under my car.

“The marshals asked me to get out of the car like a hundred times. But I was telling them to wait because I can restart. We did the procedure right. The team was super helpful on the radio, and we just changed our front wing and went again.”

Looking ahead to the final Feature Race of the weekend on Sunday, Villagómez is aiming to score more points.

“We know the pace is good,” he added. “In Baku anything can happen. It's really messy. A lot of 90-degree corners where two or three cars want to go side-by-side and it doesn't happen. So we'll see. We just try to do our job, try to be lucky and we'll see what happens.”

Next Up

title: Roman Bilinski on attacking Baku comeback: 'Sometimes you have to send it'
excerpt:
It was a solid start to the Baku races for Roman Bilinski, as he brought home points having lined up down the order in 13th on the grid.

The DAMS Lucas Oil driver wound up sixth by the chequered flag after an aggressive and well-judged drive into the points.

Reflecting on his morning's work, Bilinski said that it had been an enjoyable race and that it boded well for the longer Feature Races to come.

"Overall a very solid race. Seven overtakes done, which I think was really good. The pace was strong as well, so hopefully we can build on that in the Feature Race. So, definitely a positive race compared to the last few.

"The first one was with Miyata. He overtook me and straight away I wanted to get it back, and I didn't like that, so it was a good move.

"Then it was the same with Minì. As soon as he overtook me, I wanted to get it back, and with the last lap on Kush, I just risked everything, dived down the inside, and kind of had nothing to lose, to be honest.

"I thought it was really good. So, I'm really proud of those. I hope it was a good show for the people watching, because it definitely was exciting in the car.

"It's nice to be back in the points as well, but hopefully we can do that for some bigger points in the Features."

The DAMS driver hopes to secure more points across the Feature Races this weekend

After the disappointment of Qualifying and ending up outside the top 10, Bilinski paid tribute to the work the team did overnight to make improvements for Friday.

He added that he was very happy to make the most of the chances as they came, and believes there are even more opportunities on the table in the longer races with strategy to take into account too.

SPRINT RACE: Beganovic goes back-to-back in Baku

"It definitely takes a lot, because this sport is so demanding mentally and physically, but we stayed late, we worked really hard and looked at past years' data to be as well prepared as possible.

"Then I think part of Baku is you just have to send it. There's always going to be a bit of chaos, and you have to try and make sure you're in the right place at the right time, which is easier said than done.

"But I think we didn't do too bad today, and now we need to bring that into the Feature Race later. It's going to be a longer race. But hopefully we can make some good overtakes and a good strategy can put us in some solid points, anything can happen here."

title: Duerksen and Goethe penalised following Baku Sprint Race
excerpt:
Following the conclusion of today’s FIA Formula 2 Sprint Race in Baku, Joshua Duerksen and Oliver Goethe have been penalised.

Firstly, the Invicta Racing driver was alleged to have caused a collision at Turn 2 on the opening lap of the race with Car 25 of John Bennett.

After the race, the Stewards heard from both drivers and their team representatives and examined video evidence from both onboard cameras and external views of the incident.

They determined that Car 2 was wholly to blame for the collision between the two cars, breaching Appendix L, Chapter IV, Article 2 (d) of the FIA International Sporting Code.

However, they also noted a mitigating factors, including the incident occurring on the opening lap between Car 1 and Car 12 which contributed to the collision between Car 2 and Car 25.

As a result, they applied the lesser five-second time penalty. But since Duerksen did not finish the Sprint Race, this penalty has been converted into a three-place grid drop to be served in Feature Race 1.

Secondly, Oliver Goethe has also been given a 10-second time penalty for causing a collision at Turn 1 with MP Motorsport teammate Gabriele Minì and Hitech’s Ritomo Miyata.

After the race, the Stewards heard form all three drivers and an MP and Hitech team representative and examined video evidence.

They determined that Car 10 had been to blame for the collision between the two cars as he misjudged the loss of downforce from being so close and he locked his brakes, ost control and collided with Car 3 and then Car 9.

The Stewards applied the standard 10-second time penalty meaning Goethe drops from P15 to P16 in the final classification.

title: Round 12 Post Sprint Race Press Conference
excerpt:
FIA Formula 2: Hello and welcome to today's FIA Formula 2 Press Conference following the Sprint Race here at the Baku City Circuit. Joining us this morning in third place Alexander Dunne for Rodin Motorsport, in second place Laurens van Hoepen for TRIDENT and the winner of the Sprint Race this morning Dino Beganovic for DAMS Lucas Oil. Dino, congratulations, that's two wins in a row for you now. How happy are you with your performance today?

Dino Beganovic: Very happy obviously. It was a good race. I think we had very good pace today as well. We didn't get to show it all in qualifying yesterday, in both qualis but I think today's race was very good. I had a good start and got past Nikola and straight away we could build our gap and then just focus on our race. So super happy and especially coming back to Baku after last year it feels good to have another victory here.

FIA Formula 2: You mentioned the fact that you were able to break out the DRS window to those behind and especially Nikola at first. How crucial was that in your race and how confident you were to keep that up?

Beganovic: Obviously for many laps I was just monitoring the gap and making sure that there was no threat going into T1. But when I saw my chance to pull away, I tried to push quite hard and get the gap and once I had it, it was just a flat out race to the end. Obviously, the Safety Car in the end I was not a big fan of but it went well in the end, so I'm pretty happy.

FIA Formula 2: I was going to mention the final safety car in the restart with one lap to go. How nervous were you?

Beganovic: It was just about getting the restart right and then making your race again and getting in the rhythm, that's really it. But obviously I was not a big fan when it came out straight away and when I knew it was only one racing lap it just makes for chaos here in Baku. So in the end I'm happy with how it ended.

FIA Formula 2: We have two more races to go and the win today was DAMS’ fourth around Baku. Do you think we might see a fifth before the weekend ends?

Beganovic: I don't know, I hope so but we need to do a very good job to be able to do that. Obviously, the pace was very good this morning. Let's see what we can improve for the afternoon and then we will have to see but anything can happen here and obviously just gaining from where we're starting is already a good starting point.

FIA Formula 2: Congratulations, good job today. Laurens it's P2 for you this morning. You lost out at the start but you were pretty faultless otherwise. Are you happy with the result?

Laurens van Hoepen: Yeah, I am. I think overall we did a good race. The pace wasn't too bad. Dino, I think was a bit quicker than us today or in this race. Let's hope not in the Feature Race this afternoon but overall I'm happy. Of course I would have wanted to be able to fight a bit more for the win especially starting from P2 and Dino having a good start from P3 but overall we kept it clean. We didn't make any real big mistakes so overall I'm happy.

FIA Formula 2: We saw two drivers make mistakes at Turn 16 and you were able to profit from Nikola’s error. With DRS being so powerful on a straight that is so long, how much pressure is there to nail that selection of track lap after lap?

Van Hoepen: It's so important because as long as you have a good run on the straight, you're safe but as soon as you make a tiny mistake there, you're so vulnerable into T1. So you just have to nail it every lap and that puts some pressure on. Also with T18 and T19 being not the easiest corners to do with such high speed, it's tricky but also gives a good aspect for the racing.

FIA Formula 2: You look to have strong pace all the way through that race. How much confidence does that give you for both Feature Races, the first of which is going to be this afternoon?

Van Hoepen: Honestly, I think we were good but we still have some work to do. I think Dino was a bit quicker than us overall so we'll try and work a bit and then hopefully in the Feature we have even better pace and are able to go a few places up to the front.

FIA Formula 2: Well good job today and best of luck for this afternoon. Alex thank you for waiting. It's another podium finish for you with third place from P10 on the starting grid. You made up seven places in that race and were attacking from the start. Lap 1 at Turn 3 looked to be one of your best overtakes this season. Talk us through it.

Alexander Dunne: It was a really good start. I think Noel and Martinius were fighting through Turn 1 and I managed to get both of them on the exit and then in Turn 3, it was a good move but it wasn't necessarily planned. I think my brakes were a bit cold so when I hit the brakes, I didn't slow down as much as I had anticipated and I ended up arriving to the apex a lot quicker than what I wanted but it worked out and I managed to just keep it out of the wall so it was okay. But it was a strong race. Pace-wise it looked pretty good. I managed to get to P3 quite early on. I picked everyone off quite quickly and got to P3 a lot earlier than what I would have expected if I thought we were going to move forward. But then once I was in P3 I kind of felt like I got stuck a little bit. Laurens and Dino were pretty quick. I think we were evenly matched at times but for the most part I felt like I was maybe missing a little bit of pace to them, so maybe there's something we can do to improve the pace later on in the race.

FIA Formula 2: You will be starting on pole this afternoon. You must be feeling pretty optimistic following today's race about your chances heading into the rest of the weekend.

Dunne: I'm excited. Obviously, pole is the best place to start and after today and after yesterday as well or after this morning sorry I think we're in a good place. The pace clearly is very strong. Martinius finished P4 in the Sprint as well so we both moved forward together. So it should be an exciting one. I definitely think there's a couple of things still that we can do to improve the race pace to get a little bit more out of it but for sure we're in a good direction.

FIA Formula 2: You picked up the bonus points for a fastest lap today so that means seven vital points in the title battle. Do you have an eye on that at all this weekend?

Dunne: I'm not looking at the championship lead specifically but after Madrid I felt like there was a chance of making something happen so I'm going to make sure that I leave nothing out there and if the two races go the way I think they can then we should be right in the fight.

title: Rafael Câmara: 'A good start but we have to keep working hard' with points lead in reach
excerpt:

"It was a better start to the weekend than Nikola, but still, it's a long weekend from here and there are a lot of things that can happen.

"We just need to keep working hard and make sure that we don't relax. I'm feeling good, but a lot of action can happen so we'll really make sure that we are ready and can do some good races to move forward from where we started."

Though the Brazilian is set to start ahead of his title rival in both the Feature Races, Câmara says that there was time left on the table, especially in the second Qualifying segment.

The Invicta driver is set to line up inside the top five in both Feature Races in Baku

title: Round 12 Post Qualifying 2 Press Conference
excerpt:
FIA Formula 2: Hello again, this time for the FIA Formula 2 post-Qualifying 2 Press Conference here at Baku City Circuit. Joining us in third place, Rafael Câmara from Invicta Racing. In second place, Alexander Dunne for Rodin Motorsport and, also for Rodin Motorsport, taking his first pole position of 2026, Martinius Stenshorne. Martinius, welcome back to this couch. The roles are reversed in Qualifying 2. You lead the Rodin one-two. Congratulations. Can you tell us about that lap? You were flying.

Martinius Stenshorne: Yeah, the lap was pretty good. Also, I managed to get a good tow. It was perfect. Good strategy from the team as well to box and get one final lap on another set. So, I think we really maximised our session and we improvised well with the strategy. So, really happy.

FIA Formula 2: Were you able to take anything from that first qualifying session and use it in the second, despite the quick turnaround?

Stenshorne: Yeah, well, you find the limits and then it doesn’t change too much. Obviously, we go a bit quicker, there’s a bit more grip and the car is a bit lighter as well. So, we took some learnings from Q1 into Q2 and left it all out there.

FIA Formula 2: You said pre-weekend that you were looking to fight for the top spots and, so far, so good. What are you expecting for the rest of the round in the races?

Stenshorne: Well, I think now we have a good starting point, so that makes life a bit easier, but there’s still a long way to go. Two long races, well, three long races in total this weekend. So there’s still a lot of work to do, but it’s a good beginning.

FIA Formula 2: A very good beginning indeed. Congrats. Alex, thank you for waiting. P2 and another strong qualifying showing for you. You had a distant tow, but was it a little bit too far back to gain pace in that final sector?

Alexander Dunne: Yeah, I think I was probably a little bit too far behind. I think, in general, my lap in Q2 was pretty bad as well. My lap in Q1 was obviously quite good, but in Q2 there were a couple of mistakes. But I think, in general, it’s a difficult track, so to do two perfect laps across both sessions is always going to be difficult. But, no, in the end, to be on the front row is not the end of the world.

FIA Formula 2: It’s a very strong day for the team and exactly the kind of performance you needed with the title race still on. What makes it so special for you out there? We know that you love street circuits, but today you really showed that this is your kind of circuit.

Dunne: Yeah, I think it’s just something I enjoy. I think pushing to the limit, being close to the walls. I think this track is also different, where you’re approaching a lot of heavy braking zones from very high speed, which you don’t necessarily have on a street circuit. So I think it tests you in a lot of different areas, but it’s really enjoyable and it’s really cool. I think I said at the beginning of the weekend that qualifying is always something that a driver enjoys the most, so the fact that we had two goes at it made it a lot of fun as well. I think it was nice that, whatever you had in Q1, you had an opportunity to go out again, push the limits again, and learn and improve on what you did in Q1. So, definitely it’s a lot of fun. I think if we could do it all the time, I’d like to keep this format because it’s really enjoyable. But the track is super cool as well.

FIA Formula 2: Thank you very much. Congratulations on a great day. Moving on to Rafael, P3 in Q2. Are you happy with that result today?

Rafael Câmara: Yeah, I think overall it was a decent qualifying. Obviously, from Q1, I think we had a good base and I was able to feel more comfortable with the car in that second qualifying. Probably, I think, with the strategy we didn’t maximise, but I’m pretty happy with where we’re starting. Here in Baku as well, there’s always plenty of action in the races, so for sure there will be a lot going on on Sunday. So let’s see how it will be.

FIA Formula 2: Speaking of strategy, we saw you were out on track, but then opted to pit rather than try for a final improvement. Was that a strategy call the team made ahead of time or one that was decided during the session?

Câmara: Yeah, I mean, in the end, I think we didn’t really maximise things. For sure, we could have done a better job. I think what we did, in a way, was not really what we needed to be there fighting for position. But, in the end, I think the first lap was good enough that we’re still in a place where we can fight. Like I said, I’m quite happy with what we did and, from there, we can grab some good points.

FIA Formula 2: Like you said, you’re in a great position in both races this weekend, even in the Sprint Race. You must be feeling good about your chances of overturning the points deficit in the title race. You are seven points behind Tsolov at the moment.

Câmara: Yeah, for sure. In qualifying, we were better than him and, for sure, it gives us a better chance already with the starting positions. But we know how he is too, and we know that a lot of things can happen. So, for sure, we need to keep focused, keep our heads down, and the championship is still far from over. I think we just need to keep focusing on ourselves, make sure that we always try to maximise what we can and don’t leave anything on the table because we know how competitive he is. We always need to be there and be consistent to make sure that we can fight for the championship

title: Mari Boya: 'More to come' as he eyes triple score following best qualifying of 2026
excerpt:
Mari Boya was very happy with his and PREMA Racing's efforts in Baku Qualifying, finishing up P6 and P4 in sessions one and two respectively.

The Spaniard was even eying up a better result as he completed his lap in Q2 without a slipstream down the main start/finish straight.

Boya was pleased despite the potential left on the table, explaining that things were smooth from the first lap in Practice for PREMA in Baku.

"I'm feeling super good," he said in the paddock after the sessions. "It's a feeling I would say I forgot about. But I think there's still something in there. I needed this result, it's my first time in Baku and I think the momentum from Madrid is helping, but as I said, we've had a lot of transition in the team.

"For a driver, it's tough because you need to adapt to the category but now we're pushing a lot, and every week we are improving.

"I felt we deserved a top ten in qualifying, maybe two rounds earlier. Even with bad luck, we were fighting here, and I think we proved we can be at the front. Being alone on a track without much slipstream, I feel even better.

Boya says that there is pace to unlock in the car between Thursday and Friday

"And also around a super technical track, and again, it’s new for me. It's something I'm really proud of. There's a lot of work behind the scenes and now it's starting to pay off. I'm the same guy from the beginning of the season, simply with a better environment around me."

PREMA opted to put Boya in clean air for his final run instead of getting involved in the games between multiple drivers for track position.

Though he lost out on a tow to the line, it meant his lap was down to pure pace, something he says is looking good this weekend.

title: Round 12 Post Qualifying 1 Press Conference
excerpt:
FIA Formula 2: Hello and welcome to today’s FIA Formula 2 post-Qualifying 1 Press Conference here at Baku City Circuit. Joining us in third place, Noel León for Campos Racing. In second place, Martinius Stenshorne for Rodin Motorsport, and, for the first time on Pole Position in 2026, Alexander Dunne, also for Rodin Motorsport. Alex, congratulations. Finally, Pole Position in Feature Race 1, you’ve been quick all day. How happy are you right now?

Alexander Dunne: I’m very happy. I think this is probably the first time I’ve properly smiled all year. No, I mean, I’m very, very pleased. I think, obviously, it shows that the team have done a fantastic job with the car as well. The fact that we were one-two in both qualifying sessions, I think, obviously, as drivers, we did a good job, but in terms of team performance, that’s also pretty impressive from the team side as well. So I think credit goes just as much to them as it does to myself. So, I’m very happy. I think to finally have the opportunity to put it all together and put it on pole feels really nice.

FIA Formula 2: Track position was a key factor in the sessions today. How difficult is that to manage from the car?

Dunne: It’s quite tricky. I think, at least on my side, I was always behind someone, but I never really had the perfect slipstream. I think the slipstream I had in Q1 was a lot better than what I had in Q2. But then it’s always difficult to manage because if you’re behind someone who’s maybe a little bit slower than you, then through the lap you might end up closer than what you’d ideally like to be, which compromises sector two, but then you gain it back in sector three. So, it was quite tricky. There was a lot more of a traffic jam, let’s say, than what I expected. I think in Q1, coming out of Turn 6, we were all in a line and, at one point, I thought there was going to be a crash because everyone was going so slow. In Q2, it was the same thing coming out of 15, I think it is, or 16, where a lot of people slowed down. So it was quite difficult to manage. I would say here it was probably more difficult than Monza because here I would say slipstream is even more important than Monza, and Monza is the one that everyone talks about for traffic management and things like that. So, it was surprisingly more difficult than what it was last year. But in the end, a pole and a P2, I can’t really complain, that’s for sure.

FIA Formula 2: You keep your title hopes going with two more points for Pole Position and a chance for a first victory this season. It has eluded you so far. Are you feeling confident about finally ticking that off tomorrow?

Dunne: Yeah, I think it’s a good way to go about the end of the year, or towards the end of the year. I think after Madrid, it was kind of the first weekend where it all came together again, and we made good progress in terms of catching the guys in the championship. The gap is still relatively big, but I think after that weekend I said I’ll make sure I leave nothing out there for the rest of the season and try to close the gap as much as possible. So far, we’ve started in a good way, but we can just do what we can do. What will be, will be. We’ve done a good job in qualifying and hopefully we can continue that in the races, and then we’ll see where we end up.

FIA Formula 2: Moving on to you, Martinius. It’s P2 for you in Q1, it’s a one-two for Rodin Motorsport and, yet again, you look quick around Baku. You seem to really like this place, don’t you?

Martinius Stenshorne: Yeah, so far we’ve been really quick here. Obviously, I did my first race weekend in Formula 2 last year and that went quite well. We were really competitive. So, yeah, today as well, already from Free Practice, I felt quite confident and I think we showed our pace in qualifying.

FIA Formula 2: Do you think Pole Position was on the table in Q1? You had a tow to the finish line, but getting the perfect track position looked very tricky, at least in Q1 for you.

Stenshorne: Yeah, it was tricky. I mean, no one wants to be in front, which is understandable, and I think it was possible. I had a really good tow, but I think I could have done a bit better in the middle sector there. But in Q2 it all came together and we did everything perfectly.

FIA Formula 2: You said earlier that you had your first F2 race last year at this track and it was good, but you didn’t get the results you deserved. Do you feel like this year is your time to shine?

Stenshorne: Yeah, I hope so. Last year we were really competitive. Unfortunately, we had some issues in both races while being in contention for big points. So, yeah, hopefully this year it turns around and we get it.

FIA Formula 2: Thank you very much. Noel, it’s third place for you in Q1. You managed to find an improvement when a lot of other drivers looked to be struggling to extract another lap. How tough was your session?

Noel León: A bit, to be honest. It was a bit tough to manage the traffic. Everybody was trying to look for a slipstream and it’s quite important. So, at the end of the day, I’m happy with my lap. I think my slipstream wasn’t the best for Q1 and I think we missed pole because of that, but I’m very happy with the performance of the car and the team, and it’s a good position for tomorrow.

FIA Formula 2: Obviously, since the summer, you have been in very good form at this stage of the season. Do you feel that way as well, and do you feel like you’re keeping the momentum through Baku again?

León: Yes, I think so. We had a couple of tough weekends in the summer. Things just didn’t come my way, some stuff was not on my side and I just couldn’t get away from that. So I’m happy that, after Budapest, everything is coming nicely and going better every time. We’ll just keep the momentum until the end of the season. So, yeah, very happy with the progress and we’ll keep pushing.

FIA Formula 2: Tomorrow, you’ll be starting from the clean side of the grid. What will it take to add another win to your tally in 2026?

León: Yeah, I mean, these guys are pretty quick. You can see that they qualified one and two in both qualifying sessions. So it’s going to be tough, I think. As I said, I’m very happy with my lap and with the performance of the team because, in the morning, we didn’t look as strong as we are now. So we are making steps. We’ll try to make another one for tomorrow and we’ll see. These guys, they’re fast. I’ll let you know about that.

title: Gabriele Minì disqualified from Baku Practice
excerpt:
Following the conclusion of FIA Formula 2 Practice in Baku, MP Motorsport driver Gabriele Minì has been disqualified.

Car 9 was summoned to the Stewards after the FIA Technical Delegate reported that an insufficient quantity of fuel remained in the car post-session.

The team could not provide the required 0.8Kg fuel sample after Practice, a potential breach of Article 6.3.1 of the 2026 FIA Formula 2 Technical Regulations.

The Stewards heard from an MP Motorsport team representative and ruled that there was no justifiable reason for the infringement and breach of the Technical Regulations.

As a result, Car 9 is disqualified from the results.

title: Herta enjoying ‘technical’ Baku challenge after positive Free Practice
excerpt:
Colton Herta was happy with his pace after finishing fourth fastest in the Baku Free Practice

Colton Herta described his first 45 minutes of driving around the Baku City Circuit as “enjoyable” but now turns his focus to making sure he can have a good result this weekend.

The Hitech driver showed good form in Free Practice, finishing fourth in the timesheets, 0.495s away from pacesetter Kush Maini’s time.

Speaking in the paddock afterwards, Herta was feeling positive about his first few laps in Azerbaijan.

“It's interesting, I think it's quite technical,” said Herta describing the track. “A lot of really big brake zones, which can be difficult on the street circuit with the bumps and whatnot.

“But it's very enjoyable, I liked it. I like all the tracks this year, they've been enjoyable to drive, and they each have their own little niches in what makes them tick.

“This one is no different. It's very enjoyable, it was very dirty, so it'll be interesting to see the evolution going into qualifying.”

Herta was impressed with the layout of the Baku City Circuit

On the performance so far, Herta was speaking after debriefing with the team, and said so far things are looking positive.

“I was happy with the lap that I did,” he continued. “Obviously, I always want more, and there's still quite a bit to find if you want to be quickest.

READ MORE

‘The car is really quick’ – Maini hails strong start in Baku after going fastest in FP

“So that's kind of what we're working on in between Practice and Qualifying here, to try to set ourselves up as best as possible. There’s a lot of points on offer this weekend, but more so I would just like to get a result.”

Looking ahead to Qualifying later today, conditions are expected to be quite different.

Formula 1 will have their Free Practice before the session, which should improve the grip levels, while temperatures are expected to be warmer. In addition to that, the teams are set to run the Supersoft tyres for the first time.

The Hitech driver wants to deliver a good result this weekend

Herta says all these added factors mean he has a few things to look over before hitting the track.

“I mean, I’m trying to understand really kind of what the difference is,” he said. I want to understand what needs to happen from the driving side of things to get the lap time out of the car.

“I don't think it changes too much as far as the technique from practice. But there's obviously a lot more grip to have.

READ MORE

PRACTICE: Maini and ART Grand Prix quickest in opening Baku session

“So preparing for that and understanding where the biggest jumps come throughout the lap is important.”

Speaking further about his hopes of getting a good result, Herta added: "Every weekend you get more comfortable, and I think on these race weekends, there's really no time to learn.

“You have to be on the pace immediately because of the amount of track time. You then have a bit of a break and are able to understand a little bit more going into these last few rounds.”

Next Up

title: ‘The car is really quick’ – Maini hails strong start in Baku after going fastest in FP
excerpt:
Kush Maini was pleased to have finished fastest in the Baku Free Practice

Kush Maini was impressed with his and his ART Grand Prix team’s start to Round 12 in Baku, as he topped the times in Free Practice.

The Indian driver made a fast start to the session by setting the early benchmark, and with each lap he completed, was a constant presence near the top of the leaderboard.

But with his final lap of the 45-minute outing, Maini completed a 1:56.532 to beat Alexander Dunne to the top time by 0.204s.

Speaking after jumping out of the cockpit, Maini said: “It was really strong. I think all session we were really strong.

“It's a good feeling after Madrid obviously. We were P1 in Madrid as well after Practice and didn't end up racing really. So, nice to be back here in the front.

Maini was fastest in this morning's Free Practice

“Like we said, we know the pace is there. It's just about putting everything together now. It's great to start a doubleheader with good pace, but quali is next and practice means nothing really. So, we'll just take the confidence in the quali and try and re-deliver.

“I mean, the car is very good. It always has been. I think generally me as well, I get up to speed quite quick, even from my first day in F2.

READ MORE

PRACTICE: Maini and ART Grand Prix quickest in opening Baku session

PREVIEW: A supersized weekend in Baku for Round 12

“But I think it's a good starting point and it's time to re-do it again and try and find some time. Everyone's going to find time and quali will be interesting.”

Looking ahead to Qualifying, with the temperature expected to be warmer, a step from the Soft to the Supersoft, and with more rubber laid down by Formula 1’s Free Practice 1, Maini expects a different challenge later today.

“I think obviously with the track rubbering in, it was quite dirty in FP and then the tyres and everything, it'll change the balance a bit,” he explained. “Even the temperature will change the balance a bit.

Maini is expecting a different track for Qualifying later today

“But in the end, we're in the right ballpark and it's about tweaking things. I think from the experience from previous years, we can sort of expect what change is going to be made and from a driving point as well, it's going to be a step forward.

“So, let's see. We know what it takes to get forward. That's pretty good.”

On the fight for pole, Maini who already has two Aramco Pole Position Awards this season – from Miami and Budapest – is hopeful to get two more this evening from Qualifying 1 and 2.

“If I do my best, the car is there and we should be there,” he added. “So, that's all I need to focus on. We'll see.”

title: Martinius Stenshorne aiming for Baku rebound and return to podium
excerpt:
Rodin Motorsport's Martinius Stenshorne is eager to get back into the points this weekend around the Baku City Circuit.

The Norwegian made his FIA Formula 2 debut around the track a year ago, impressing in Qualifying to earn P7 in his first outing. He was denied points in both races due to various incidents out of his control, but returning to Baku, the Rodin driver has high hopes for this weekend.

"Last year it was mainly about just getting into the rhythm with the new car," he explained. "It was also a new track for me, so there were quite a lot of things to learn.

"Obviously this year I have a bit more experience coming here, both with the car and the track, so I'm looking forward to it.

"The most difficult thing here is the same as any other street track - the walls are so close, so finding the limit and not being over it but also not too far under it as well is tough.

After learning on the fly one year ago, Stenshorne now has a year's worth of F2 experience to rely upon, and he says that his weekend should be much more straightforward than 12 months ago.

Stenshorne is looking to return to the podium after a tricky spell during the middle part of the year

He is also eager for a good run in all three races this weekend after missing out on a scoring result due to a Safety Car that impacted his strategy and hopes of points.

"It will make it easier. I think we still showed really good pace last year, even though it was first for me. It went really well until it didn't. Hopefully we can carry that good speed into this year and have some good qualifying results and hopefully score some good points in all three races.

"We haven't scored as much as we wanted to lately. It was looking good for a while in Madrid, until another Safety Car came out and kind of ruined our strategy, so hopefully we can get some good points over the line this weekend."

He and the rest of the drivers will have an extra chance of points this weekend, with two Qualifying and Feature Races added to the expanded one-off format for Round 12.

The Rodin driver says that while it won't make much of a difference in terms of approach to the weekend, having an extra race is a welcome addition as he looks to return to the podium for the first time since the Spa Sprint Race.

"It's an extra chance to score some points. I think the preparation has been the same as it usually is, not much has changed. We did our usual sim in the factory.

"The goal now is to be on it from the beginning and pick up some good points on Saturday as well. But for sure the main goal now is to be on it from Thursday and score good points in all three races."

title: James Wharton steps up with TRIDENT for the 2027 season
excerpt:
TRIDENT have announced the signing of James Wharton for the 2027 FIA Formula 2 season.

Wharton steps up from Formula 3 after two seasons, achieving two victories and four podiums in total.

Prior to that, the Australian driver won the 2023 Formula 4 UAE Championship and finished as the runner-up in the 2024 Formula Regional European Championship.

Wharton now graduates to Formula 2 with TRIDENT, having previously raced for the Italian team at Lusail in 2025. Speaking at the announcement, he expressed his delight at the opportunity to work with them once again.

“I really can’t put into words what this opportunity for 2027 means to me,” said Wharton. “To be able to return to TRIDENT after racing with them in 2025 is something really special. We worked very well together and they are a very prestigious team that has done a great job over the last few seasons.

“I’m looking forward to joining the team and continuing to work hard with them over the winter, so that we can arrive in 2027 in the best possible shape. A huge thank you to Giacomo and Maurizio for giving me the opportunity to drive their car and be part of their team. I can’t thank TRIDENT enough, and I’m really looking forward to starting this new chapter of my career.”

TRIDENT Team Manager Giacomo Ricci added: “We are very happy to announce that James Wharton will compete in the 2027 FIA Formula 2 Championship with Trident Motorsport. We got to know him at the end of 2025, when he made his debut with us in F2, and since then we have continued to closely monitor his development. James has demonstrated speed, talent, and great determination. The season just ended allowed him to gain further experience, and we are confident that the work we will do together will enable him to take a significant step forward.”

title: What To Watch For: A few key talking points going into Baku
excerpt:
After a week’s break, the paddock is heading to Baku for Round 12 of this incredible 2026 FIA Formula 2 season.

It could be a critical few days in the title fight in what should be an action-packed few days in Azerbaijan, so we have picked out a few storylines to look for this weekend.

A NEW FORMAT

For the keen onlookers in Madrid, you will have noticed a new weekend format in Formula 3 – with two Qualifying sessions, one Sprint Race and two Feature Races.

Well we are going to have the same with Formula 2 in Baku, meaning that there are 67 points on offer this weekend.

It means the drivers will have a busy Thursday, with Free Practice kicking off the action. Later in the day there are two 20-minute back-to-back Qualifying sessions.

There will be an additional Qualifying session and Feature Race in Baku this weekend

Friday is just as jam-packed with a Sprint Race in the morning and the first Feature Race in the afternoon. All of this before they return for the final race on Saturday.

This will be another test for the drivers as well as their teams as it will be a busy few days. But if it goes well, with the number of points on offer, it could be very rewarding weekend.

READ MORE

How to watch Round 12 in Baku: TV, Session times and more

Inthraphuvasak: 'Points the perfect way to repay the team'

TITLE LEAD IS CRITICAL

With so many points available, those drivers in the title fight will be eager to make sure they maximise their results to give themselves the best chance of being champion.

One of the reasons is that after Baku, there is a two-month before the final two rounds in Lusail and Yas Marina.

An interesting fact is that in the previous nine seasons of Formula 2, the driver who leads the Championship with two rounds to go has gone on to win the title.

The fight to be top at the end of the Baku weekend could be tight

Maybe it will be 10th time lucky for the chasing pack this year, but history shows that you want to be ahead at this time of the season.

With 67 points on offer, a bad weekend for any of the contenders, and a strong performance from their rivals could put them on the back foot heading into the final part of the season.

TSOLOV NEEDS A BOUNCE BACK

At one stage this season Nikola Tsolov could not be stopped. He achieved six victories in the first seven rounds but the four race weekends since have not been as smooth.

The Campos Racing driver still leads the Drivers’ Championship but since his double wins at Silverstone, he has just one podium and two DNFs.

But the inherit pace in each of those race weekends has still been quite strong for Tsolov and Campos, so they will not be too worried.

However, as previously said, the driver that wins the title tends to be the leader going into the final two rounds, so history tells us that is key for Tsolov to maintain his place at the top.

But Rafael Câmara is just seven points behind and with Gabriele Minì and Alexander Dunne having closed the gap in Madrid, Tsolov has a fight on his hands for the championship.

Duerksen has the chance to make history in Baku this weekend

DUERKSEN AIMING FOR HISTORY

There are many drivers in this championship aiming to make history of their own but maybe none are currently as close as Joshua Duerksen.

The Invicta Racing driver returns to Baku – the scene of his first F2 victory in 2024 – with desires on having the outright record for the most wins in the championship.

After Duerksen’s Feature Race victory in Monza, he tied Artem Markelov, Nyck de Vries, Richard Verschoor and Felipe Drugovich on eight wins.

READ MORE

Gabriele Minì: 'Title not out of reach' after aggressive drive to points in Madrid

A victory at the venue where it all started would be a great way to own that record, and based on his history in Baku, it is very possible.

As well as the win in 2024, Duerksen finished second in the Feature Race last season – after starting in P14.

So look out for the Paraguayan this weekend, who has already said he wants that record for himself.
